What single word names the practice of banning by law the making, selling, and drinking of alcoholic beverages?
The oldest of 14 children born to Palestinian immigrants in Detroit, this congresswoman became the first Palestinian American woman elected to Congress in 2018 — who is she?
Rashida Tlaib: American politician and lawyer (born 1976)
Co-leading Germany's Greens alongside Annalena Baerbock, this politician served as Vice Chancellor and climate minister under Chancellor Olaf Scholz — who is he?

Over three days in September 1982, Lebanese Forces militiamen — backed by the IDF — killed thousands of mostly Palestinian and Shia civilians in a Beirut neighbourhood and adjacent refugee camp; what is this atrocity called?
Sabra and Shatila massacre: 1982 mass murder of civilians in Beirut, Lebanon.
This Finnish lawyer chaired the National Coalition Party from 1994 to 2001 and later served as president from 2012 to 2024, defeating Pekka Haavisto in a 2012 runoff — who is he?
Sauli Niinistö: President of Finland from 2012 to 2024. Sauli Väinämö Niinistö (born 24 August 1948) is a Finnish politician who served as the president of Finland from 2012 to 2024.
Centered on Marib and Sirwah in what's now Yemen, this ancient kingdom was considered the birthplace of South Arabian civilization and once expanded into the Horn of Africa. Which kingdom?
Sheba: Ancient South Arabian kingdom. Sheba, or Saba, was an ancient South Arabian kingdom that existed in Yemen before 275 CE.
An architect by training who once served as mayor of Quito, this man won Ecuador's presidency on his third try in 1992 after founding a new conservative party — who is it?
Sixto Durán Ballén: President of Ecuador from 1992 to 1996.
Established by Seljuk Turks after their victory over Byzantine forces at Manzikert in 1071, this Turco-Persian state is considered the beginning of Turkish history in Anatolia. What was it?
Sultanate of Rum: Turkish state in central Anatolia from 1077 to 1308.
This biblical figure, son of Nahor, is best known as the father of the patriarch Abraham in the Book of Genesis — who is he?
Terah: Figure in the Hebrew Bible; son of Nahor.
The eighth shogun of his family's shogunate, ruling from 1716 to 1745, this samurai is remembered for repealing Japan's ban on Western literature — who was he?
Tokugawa Yoshimune: Japanese Samurai, Daimyo and Military ruler of Japan from 1716 to 1745.

Exemplified by thinkers like Saint-Simon, Fourier, and Robert Owen, this early-19th-century current imagined ideal, non-capitalist societies but was later dismissed by Marxists as impractical — what is it called?
Utopian socialism: Political theory concerned with imagined socialist societies.
Before leading a nation through a full-scale invasion, this law graduate co-founded a comedy company called Kvartal 95 — which president took office in 2019?
Volodymyr Zelenskyy: President of Ukraine since 2019.

A vaudeville-trained humorist born a citizen of the Cherokee Nation and known as 'Oklahoma's Favorite Son,' he made 71 films and wrote over 4,000 newspaper columns before dying in a 1935 plane crash — who was he?
Will Rogers: American humorist and entertainer (1879–1935)
This Pakistani general became the country's third president under martial law in 1969, and his tenure oversaw the war that led to Bangladesh's independence — who was he?
Yahya Khan: President of Pakistan from 1969 to 1971.
Serving first as Albania's youngest-ever prime minister at 27, then president, then finally crowning himself monarch in 1928, this statesman ruled the country until 1939 — who was he?
Zog I: Leader of Albania from 1922 to 1939.
Which of these four was born earliest?
Eratosthenes (born 276 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
Eratosthenes (born 276 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four began earliest?
Python (programming language) (founded 1991) is the earliest of the four. Python supports multiple programming paradigms but with an emphasis on object-oriented programming and dynamic typing.
Which one below was established earliest?
MATLAB (founded 1984) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below is best known as a physicist?
Robert Boyle is a physicist. Robert Boyle (25 January 1627 – 31 December 1691) was an Anglo-Irish natural philosopher, chemist, physicist, alchemist and inventor.
Pick the chemist from these four.
James Lovelock is a chemist. James Ephraim Lovelock (26 July 1919 – 26 July 2022) was an English independent scientist, environmentalist and futurist.
What is the atomic number of Neodymium?
Neodymium is a chemical element; it has symbol Nd and atomic number 60.
In what year was Pythagoras born?
Pythagoras: Pythagoras of Samos (Ancient Greek: Πυθαγόρας; c. 570 – c. 495 BC) was an ancient Ionian Greek philosopher, polymath, and the eponymous founder of Pythagoreanism.
In what year was Elon Musk born?
Elon Musk: Elon Reeve Musk (EE-lon; born June 28, 1971) is a businessman and former public official who is the CEO and largest shareholder of Tesla and SpaceX.
In what year was Armin Meiwes born?
Armin Meiwes: After Meiwes and the victim jointly attempted to eat the victim's severed penis, Meiwes murdered his victim and proceeded to eat a large amount of his flesh.
In what year did Mohamed Atta die?
Mohamed Atta: In Hamburg, Atta attended prayers at the al-Quds Mosque where he met Marwan al-Shehhi, Ramzi bin al-Shibh, and Ziad Jarrah, with whom he formed the Hamburg cell.
In what year did Nostradamus die?
Nostradamus's father's family had originally been Jewish, but had converted to Catholic Christianity a generation before Nostradamus was born.
In what year was Silver discovered?
Silver is a chemical element; it has symbol Ag (from Latin argentum 'silver') and atomic number 47.
In what year was Manganese discovered?
Manganese is a chemical element; it has the symbol Mn and atomic number 25.
Which company manufactures LTV A-7 Corsair II?
LTV A-7 Corsair II: Ling-Temco-Vought. The LTV A-7 Corsair II is an American carrier-capable subsonic light attack aircraft designed and manufactured by Ling-Temco-Vought (LTV).
Which country is Sukhoi Su-57 from?
Sukhoi Su-57: Russia. The Sukhoi Su-57 (Russian: Сухой Су-57; NATO reporting name: Felon) is a twin-engine stealth multirole fighter aircraft developed by Sukhoi.
Who is credited with discovering Grus?
Grus (constellation): Petrus Plancius. Grus (or colloquially) is a constellation in the southern sky.
Who is credited with discovering Reynolds number?
Reynolds number: Sir George Stokes, 1st Baronet. At low Reynolds numbers, flows tend to be dominated by laminar (sheet-like) flow, while at high Reynolds numbers, flows tend to be turbulent.
Who is credited with discovering Ceres?
Ceres (dwarf planet): Giuseppe Piazzi. Ceres is a dwarf planet in the main asteroid belt between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
This localized collection of pus builds up within body tissue, usually from bacterial infection, causing redness, pain, warmth, and swelling. What is it?
Abscess is a collection of pus that has built up within the tissue of the body, usually caused by bacterial infection.
A pioneer of industrial toxicology, this American physician trained at Michigan, worked out of Hull House in Chicago, and led the fight to curb lead poisoning in the workplace — who was she?
Alice Hamilton (February 27, 1869 - September 22, 1970) was an American physician, research scientist, and author.

Native to tropical America and carried across the Pacific by Spanish traders aboard the Manila galleons, this small tree in the same family as soursop produces a scaly-skinned fruit with sweet, creamy flesh — what's the species?
Annona squamosa is a small, well-branched tree or shrub from the family Annonaceae that bears edible fruits called sugar apples or sweetsops or custard apples.

Explicitly describing the relativity of motion and, by his own account, 23 years old in 499 CE, this figure is considered the first of the great mathematician-astronomers of classical Indian science — who is he?
Aryabhata (476-550 CE) was the first of the major mathematician-astronomers and early physicist from the classical age of Indian mathematics and Indian astronomy.

An Arctic and sub-Arctic cetacean, it is one of two living members of the family Monodontidae and is also known as the white whale (the only cetacean regularly occurring with this color) and the sea canary for its high-pitched calls. What is it?
Beluga whale (Delphinapterus leucas), is an Arctic and sub-Arctic cetacean.
This leafy vegetable forms no head, just green blades atop pale bulbous stalks, with a flavor often compared to a mix of spinach and water chestnut — what vegetable is it?

Bok choy (American English, Canadian English, and Australian English), pak choi (British English, South African English, and Caribbean English) or pok choi is a type of Chinese cabbage (Brassica rapa subsp.
Unlike ordinary weight loss from undereating, this illness-linked syndrome strips away muscle mass in ways good nutrition can't fully undo — what condition is it?
Cachexia is a syndrome that occurs in people with certain illnesses, causing muscle loss that cannot be fully reversed with improved nutrition.
This clouding of the eye's lens is responsible for nearly 40 percent of blindness cases worldwide, often causing halos around lights and trouble seeing at night — what condition is it?
Cataract is a cloudy area in the lens of the eye that impairs vision.
Linked to repeated head trauma, this worsening neurodegenerative disease turns up in boxers and footballers — and even in soccer players, largely from heading the ball. What is it?

Chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) is a neurodegenerative disease linked to repeated trauma to the head. The encephalopathy symptoms can include behavioral problems, mood problems, and problems with thinking.
This group of mostly evergreen, cone-bearing trees and shrubs reproduces via wind-pollination, with the seeds themselves also scattered by the wind — what plant group is it?
Conifer are a group of vascular plants and a subset of gymnosperms.
Native to Mexico and Central America and related to the sunflower and daisy, this genus of 49 tuberous perennial species blooms in nearly every color except blue — which genus?
Dahlia is a genus of bushy, tuberous, herbaceous perennial plants native to Mexico and Central America.
Tamed in Africa millennia ago and still hauling loads across the developing world, which equine traces its lineage to Equus africanus?
Donkey is a domesticated equine. It was domesticated in Africa some 5000–7000 years ago, and has been used mainly as a working animal since that time.
Born to a mathematician father in Erlangen, this pioneering algebraist proved theorems connecting symmetry to conservation laws in physics — who is she?
Emmy Noether (23 March 1882 - 14 April 1935) was a German mathematician who made many important contributions to abstract algebra.

This front-of-the-head feature found in humans and other animals houses most of the sense organs, including the eyes, nose, and mouth, and its damage can profoundly affect one's sense of identity — name this body part?
Face is the front of the head in humans and many other animals that features most of the sense organs including the eyes, nose and mouth.
This Italian-American economist, who taught at MIT's Sloan School, took home the 1985 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economics. Who was he?
Franco Modigliani (18 June 1918 - 25 September 2003) was an Italian-American economist and the recipient of the 1985 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economics.

He shared a 1951 Nobel for synthesizing ten transuranium elements and developed the actinide concept that reshaped the periodic table; this American chemist later advised ten US presidents on nuclear policy — who was he?

Glenn T. Seaborg (April 19, 1912 - February 25, 1999) was an American chemist whose involvement in the synthesis, discovery and investigation of ten transuranium elements earned him a share of the 1951 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
Prehensile and multi-fingered, this appendage sits at the end of primates' forearms, though a few other animals like koalas and raccoons are sometimes described as having one too — which body part?
Hand is a prehensile, multi-fingered appendage located at the end of the forearm or forelimb of primates such as humans, chimpanzees, monkeys, and lemurs.
Originally a variable measure equal to one-twelfth of the night or day in the ancient Near East, this unit of time is now fixed at exactly 3,600 seconds — name this unit?
Hour (symbol: h; also abbreviated hr) is a unit of time historically reckoned as 124 of a day and defined contemporarily as exactly 3,600 seconds.
This contagious bacterial skin infection most often shows up as yellowish crusts on a child's face, arms, or legs, and spreads easily in crowded day cares and contact sports — what is it?
Impetigo is a contagious bacterial infection that involves the superficial skin.

This Swiss psychologist's theory of cognitive development, paired with his epistemological views, is together known as genetic epistemology, and remains foundational in early-childhood education. Who is he?
Jean Piaget (9 August 1896 - 16 September 1980) was a Swiss psychologist known for his work on child development.
Arrested in 1995 for various computer crimes and imprisoned for five years, this convicted hacker later became a computer-security consultant and author — who is he?
Kevin Mitnick (August 6, 1963 - July 16, 2023) was an American computer security consultant, author, and convicted hacker.
This bacterial blood infection, spread between humans, dogs, and rodents, can range from symptomless to a severe form that turns skin and eyes yellow and shuts down the kidneys — what disease is it?
Leptospirosis is a blood infection caused by bacteria of the genus Leptospira that can infect humans, dogs, rodents, and many other wild and domesticated animals.
Born in Vienna into one of Europe's richest families, this philosopher studied under Bertrand Russell at Cambridge and transformed 20th-century philosophy of language and logic — who is he?

Ludwig Wittgenstein ((h)tyne; Austrian; 26 April 1889 - 29 April 1951) was an Austro-British philosopher who worked in logic, philosophy of mathematics, philosophy of mind, and philosophy of language.
Often called the 'father of the handheld cell phone,' this Motorola engineer placed the first public mobile call in 1973 from a New York City sidewalk — who is he?
Martin Cooper (inventor) (born December 26, 1928) is an American engineer.

An advanced modification of the Korean War-era MiG-15, this Soviet transonic fighter jet entered production in 1952, was license-built in both China and Poland, and remains in North Korean service today — what's the aircraft?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-17 (NATO reporting name: Fresco) is a transonic fighter aircraft that was produced in the Soviet Union from 1952 and was operated by air forces internationally.
Caused by antibodies blocking acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction, this autoimmune disease most often weakens the muscles of the eyes, face and throat — which disease?
Myasthenia gravis (MG) is a long-term neuromuscular junction disease that leads to varying degrees of skeletal muscle weakness.

Made from unleavened dough rolled flat and then cut, stretched, or extruded into long strips, this staple food appears across cultures — in Italian cuisine, it goes by an entirely different name. What is it, generically?
Noodle are a type of food typically made from unleavened dough which is rolled flat and cut, stretched, or extruded into long strips or strings.
Dubbed the father of nuclear chemistry, he studied under Ernest Rutherford before helping identify the radioactive elements radium, thorium, and protactinium — who is he?
Otto Hahn (8 March 1879 - 28 July 1968) was a German chemist who was a pioneer in the field of radiochemistry.

A Chinese singer famous for annual appearances on a widely watched Lunar New Year television gala, she has served as her country's First Lady since 2012 as the wife of its paramount leader — who is she?

Peng Liyuan (pinyin: Png Lyun; born 20 November 1962) is a Chinese singer who has served as the First Lady of China since 2012, as the wife of Xi Jinping, the General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party and paramount leader of China.
Which condition, more common in people with obesity or a family history, involves hair and skin debris being drawn into tissue through tiny skin openings called pits?
Pilonidal disease is a type of skin infection that typically occurs as a cyst between the cheeks of the buttocks and often at the upper end.
Used to disinfect both healthcare workers' hands and patients' skin before and after surgery, this antiseptic can be applied as a liquid, ointment, or powder — which compound?

Povidone-iodine is an antiseptic used for skin disinfection before and after surgery. Povidone-iodine (PVP-I), also known as iodopovidone, is an antiseptic used for skin disinfection before and after surgery.
Used to treat malaria and babesiosis, this medication also gives tonic water its distinctive bitter taste — what is it?
Quinine is a medication used to treat malaria and babesiosis. While sometimes used for nocturnal leg cramps, quinine is not recommended for this purpose due to the risk of serious side effects.
First created near Darmstadt in 1994 and named for the physicist who discovered X-rays, this extremely radioactive element exists as only a handful of atoms with no practical use — which one is it?
Roentgenium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Rg and atomic number 111.
Found on every continent but Antarctica and numbering over 2,500 species, this eight-legged arachnid curves a stinger-tipped tail over its back — what is it?

Scorpion (order Scorpiones) are predatory arachnids with eight legs, a pair of grasping pincers (or Chelae) and a narrow, segmented tail, often carried in a characteristic forward curve over the back and always ending with a stinger.
This vertebrate organ system serves three main functions, protection, regulation, and sensation, and in mammals is made of multiple layers of ectodermal tissue. What is it?

Skin is the layer of usually soft, flexible outer tissue covering the body of a vertebrate animal, with three main functions: protection, regulation, and sensation. The adjective cutaneous means "of the skin" (from Latin cutis 'skin').

Described as the most extreme form of malnutrition, this severe shortfall of caloric energy is so grave that deliberately inflicting it on a population is a crime under international law — what is it?
Starvation is a severe deficiency in caloric energy intake, below the level needed to maintain an organism's life.
These large, often hairy spiders of the family Theraphosidae number over a thousand species, and New World pet varieties can flick irritating 'urticating hairs' at threats. What creatures are they?
Tarantula are a group of large and often hairy spiders of the family Theraphosidae.

Proposing an information management system in March 1989 and implementing the first successful client-server exchange that November, this English computer scientist invented HTML, HTTP and the URL system — who is he?
Tim Berners-Lee (born 8 June 1955), also known as TimBL, is an English computer scientist best known as the inventor of the World Wide Web, HTML, the URL system, and HTTP.
What is the medical term for having dangerously high levels of urea in the blood, typically caused by kidney failure?

Uremia is the condition of having high levels of urea in the blood. It is the signs, symptoms and results from laboratory tests which result from inadequate excretory, regulatory, and endocrine function of the kidneys.
His 1925 Umdeutung paper reinterpreted old quantum theory, and two years later he published a famous uncertainty principle — which German physicist was he?

Werner Heisenberg (5 December 1901 - 1 February 1976) was a German theoretical physicist, one of the main pioneers of the theory of quantum mechanics and a principal scientist in the German nuclear program during World War II.
Also known as the empirical guideline, this statistical shorthand describes the percentage of values within one, two, and three standard deviations of the mean in a normal distribution — which one?
Transmitted by the bite of an infected tsetse fly, this parasitic infection caused by Trypanosoma brucei is better known in humans as 'sleeping sickness' — what's its formal name?
African trypanosomiasis: Parasitic disease also known as sleeping sickness.

This exaggerated immune response occurs when the body mistakes a harmless substance for a threat, triggering histamine release from mast cells and conditions like hay fever or anaphylaxis. What is this reaction called?
Allergy: Immune system response to a substance that most people tolerate well.
Considered the father of the exact and natural sciences in Armenia, this 7th-century polymath wrote the first known Armenian geographic work — who was he?
This psychological state describes a lack of feeling, motivation, or concern, sitting on a spectrum between normal drive and akinetic mutism — what is it called?
Apathy: State of indifference, or the suppression of emotions.

With the symbol At and atomic number 85, this is the rarest naturally occurring element in Earth's crust, so radioactive that a macroscopic sample would instantly vaporize itself — what element is it?
Astatine: Chemical element with atomic number 85 (At). It is the rarest naturally occurring element in the Earth's crust, occurring only as the decay product of various heavier elements.

The most widespread bird in its family, found on every continent except Antarctica (where only stray vagrants appear), this species has blue upperparts, a deeply forked tail, and usually nests in man-made structures — what is it?
Barn swallow: Species of bird. The barn swallow (Hirundo rustica) is the most widespread species of swallow in the world, occurring on all continents, with vagrants reported even in Antarctica.
This English musician played bass on the Rolling Stones' first nineteen studio albums across three decades before later fronting his own blues outfit, the Rhythm Kings — who is he?
Developed alongside the 707 airliner from the same prototype, this narrower, shorter jet became the U.S. Air Force's first jet-powered refueling tanker in 1957 — name the aircraft?
Boeing KC-135 Stratotanker: US military aerial refueling and transport aircraft.
Sold under the brand name Pulmicort, this steroid drug treats asthma when inhaled but also comes as a nasal spray for allergies and a rectal foam for bowel disease — which medication?
This highly contagious virus, spread through feces, can kill up to 91% of untreated dogs and wolves and also strikes foxes, cats, and skunks — what is it?
Canine parvovirus: Contagious virus mainly affecting dogs.
Native to Madagascar, this flowering plant known as the Madagascar periwinkle is the source of two major cancer-fighting drugs — what is it?
Catharanthus roseus: Species of flowering plant in the family Apocynaceae.
Its roasted root has long served as a coffee substitute, while today its extracted inulin shows up as a sweetener and fiber additive in packaged foods — which blue-flowered plant?
Chicory: Flowering plant in the daisy family.
Found in birds, reptiles, amphibians, and egg-laying mammals like the platypus, which single all-purpose body opening handles digestion, reproduction, and waste?
The heaviest songbird on Earth and the most widely distributed of all the corvids, this all-black passerine averages 25 inches long across the Northern Hemisphere — what is it?
Common raven: Large, black species of passerine bird.
First described in 1963, this rare disorder from a partial deletion on chromosome 5 gets its French name from the distinctive feline-sounding cry of affected infants — what is it called?
Cri du chat syndrome: Human medical condition.

This English broadcaster is the only person to have won BAFTA Awards in black-and-white, colour, high-definition, 3D, and 4K — a span made possible by a presenting career that began with Zoo Quest in 1954. Who is this natural historian?
David Attenborough: English broadcaster and natural historian (born 1926)

A lean, wedge-skulled medium canine found in Australia and split off from the New Guinea singing dog, this animal's very classification — dog, wolf, or its own species — is still hotly debated — what is it?
Dingo: Canid species native to Australia.

Anatomically like us, some of the oldest remains of this species come from Ethiopia's Omo-Kibish site, dated to roughly 233,000 to 196,000 years ago — what term distinguishes them from archaic humans?
Early modern human: Old Stone Age ''Homo sapiens''
This inner lining of the uterus sheds during menstruation but thickens dramatically to help form the placenta during pregnancy — what is it?
Endometrium: Lining of the mammalian uterus. It has a basal layer and a functional layer: the basal layer contains stem cells which regenerate the functional layer.
This warbler's head marking gives it its name — dark in the male, chestnut in the female — and its closest relative is the garden warbler. What bird is it?
Eurasian blackcap: Bird in the Old World warbler family from Eurasia and Africa.
This German mathematician's 1872 Erlangen program reorganized all of geometry by its underlying symmetry groups, and he later turned Göttingen into a world center of research — who was he?
Home to the radius and ulna joined by the interosseous membrane, this region of the arm lies between the elbow and the wrist — what is it?
Forearm: Region of the upper limb between the elbow and the wrist.
Naming his most famous pistol after his 17th patent — not for holding seventeen rounds, as many assume — this Austrian engineer got his design into Austrian service in 1982 — who was he?
Prince Carl Philip, Duke of Värmland

Making up about 15% of all brain tumors and thought to arise from cells called astrocytes, this aggressive cancer often announces itself only with vague headaches or sudden personality changes — what is it?
Glioblastoma: Aggressive type of brain cancer. Initial signs and symptoms of glioblastoma are nonspecific.

Native to the Amazon basin, this climbing plant's coffee-bean-sized seeds can be up to 6% caffeine — double a green coffee bean — making it a staple in Brazilian soft drinks and energy drinks — which plant?
Also known as the Burgundy snail and served as escargot, this large air-breathing land snail native to Europe has a globular brown shell — what species is it?
German anthropologist Otto Schoetensack named this archaic human species in 1908 based on a jawbone found near the village of Mauer — then Europe's oldest known human fossil. Which species?

Homo heidelbergensis: Extinct species of archaic human. H. heidelbergensis has been regarded as either the last common ancestor of modern humans, Neanderthals, and Denisovans; or as a completely separate lineage.
Formed when chlorine dissolves in water, this compound is the main disinfecting agent in chlorine solutions — and your own white blood cells make it to fight off invading germs. What is it?
Hypochlorous acid: Chemical compound. Hypochlorous acid is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula ClOH, also written as HClO, HOCl, or ClHO.

This neurological emergency is sudden bleeding directly into brain tissue or its fluid-filled cavities — not from a blocked vessel, but a burst one — causing anything from headache to sudden paralysis. What is it?
Intracerebral hemorrhage: Type of intracranial bleeding that occurs within the brain tissue itself.
He won the Fields Medal in 1954 and, nearly half a century later, the very first Abel Prize in 2003 — which French mathematician of algebraic topology and geometry is it?

Conceived as a high-speed 'Schnellbomber' for the German Luftwaffe, this twin-engined WWII aircraft evolved into everything from a night fighter to the explosive lower half of composite 'Mistel' combinations — what is it?
Junkers Ju 88: German twin-engined multirole combat aircraft.

Nicknamed 'acid' and 'Lucy' and derived from the ergot fungus, this semisynthetic hallucinogen is so potent that 20 micrograms produces noticeable effects — yet no fatal human overdose has ever been documented — what is it?
Sold under the brand name Xyzal, this less-sedating second-generation antihistamine for hay fever and hives was patented in 1965 but not approved in the US until 2007 — what is it?
Levocetirizine: Antihistamine medication. It is classified as a second-generation antihistamine and works by blocking histamine H1-receptors.
Nicknamed the sea devil, frogfish, or fishing frog, this species anchors a major commercial fishery in the Irish Sea and ranges from the Barents Sea to the Mediterranean — which fish?
Lophius piscatorius: Species of fish. Lophius piscatorius, commonly known as the angler, toadfish, sea frog, fishing frog, frogfish, or sea devil, is a species of Lophius in the family Lophiidae.
This category of health conditions arises from too few, too many, or an imbalance of nutrients, and can cause anything from stunted growth to obesity. What is it called?
Malnutrition: Medical condition caused by receiving too little or too many nutrients.

Entering US Navy service in 1961 before the Marines and Air Force adopted it too, this twin-engine supersonic jet became America's most-produced supersonic military aircraft with 5,195 built — which aircraft?
McDonnell Douglas F-4 Phantom II: Fighter aircraft family developed from 1958.
Sold as Flagyl, this antibiotic and antiprotozoal fights everything from giardiasis to trichomoniasis — but it's notorious for leaving a metallic taste in your mouth — what is it?
Metronidazole: Antibiotic and antiprotozoal medication. Metronidazole, sold under the brand name Flagyl and Metrogyl among others, is an antibiotic and antiprotozoal medication.
With shovel-like front limbs built for burrowing and a mating song broadcast from a specially shaped underground tunnel, which insect is this?
Mole cricket: Members of the insect family Gryllotalpidae.
This lipid-rich substance wraps around nerve axons in segments, leaving gaps called nodes of Ranvier that let electrical signals leap along in a process called saltatory conduction — what is it?
Myelin: Fatty substance insulating nerve cell axons.
This Renaissance polymath put the Sun, not Earth, at the center of the universe in a book published just before his death in 1543 — kicking off a revolution in science. Who was he?
This soft-bodied mollusc can radically deform its shape to squeeze through tiny gaps and propels itself backward by jetting water through a siphon — what eight-limbed creature is it?
Octopus: Soft-bodied eight-limbed order of molluscs.
Also called a steer or bullock, and usually yoked in pairs, which castrated male bovine has long served as a draft animal for ploughing and hauling?
Ox: Common bovine draft and riding animal.
This Stanford biologist became famous — and controversial — for his 1968 book warning that runaway population growth would bring famine and resource depletion. Who was he?
Turning colorless in acid and a fuchsia pink in base, this phthalein dye is a favorite indicator for acid-base titrations — what is it?
Phenolphthalein: pH indicator that turns pink in basic solution.
Its name comes from the Spanish for 'little silver,' yet this dense, stubbornly unreactive metal — element 78 — is so scarce only a few hundred tonnes are mined a year. Which one?
Platinum: Chemical element with atomic number 78 (Pt)

Arising over 60 million years ago from small tree-dwellers, this order favored big brains, binocular color vision and opposable thumbs to grasp among the branches — and it includes lemurs and apes — what is it?
Primate: Order of mammals. New primate species continue to be discovered: over 25 species were described in the 2000s, 36 in the 2010s, and six in the 2020s.

Known in France as the Patou and in the US by another name, this French livestock guardian breed hails from a range straddling France and Spain, protecting flocks from wolves and bears. What breed is it?
Pyrenean Mountain Dog: French breed of dog. The Pyrenean Mountain Dog (Chien de Montagne des Pyrénées) is a French breed of livestock guardian dog.

This Canadian-American inventor pulled off the first transmission of speech by radio in 1900 and the first two-way radiotelegraphy across the Atlantic in 1906, racking up hundreds of patents — seven granted after his death. Who was this AM-radio pioneer?
Reginald Fessenden: Canadian-American electrical engineer and inventor (1866–1932)
Commonly called the dog rose, this variable climbing wild plant is native to Europe, northwest Africa, and western Asia — which species?
Also known as mucopolysaccharidosis type III, this rare genetic disorder is caused by the body's inability to break down certain sugar molecules called glycosaminoglycans — what is it called?

Sanfilippo syndrome: Rare metabolism disorder. Sanfilippo syndrome, also known as mucopolysaccharidosis type III (MPS III), is a rare lifelong genetic disease that mainly affects the brain and spinal cord.
Born in Moscow and brought to the US at age six, this computer scientist co-founded Google with Larry Page and served as president of its parent company until 2019 — who is he?
Sometimes triggered just by stepping into bright sunlight, a quirk called the photic reflex, this involuntary, explosive expulsion of air clears irritants from the nose and mouth. What is it?
Sneeze: Semi-autonomous, convulsive expulsion of air from the lungs through the nose and mouth.
